items.title: Get a sneak-peak at Warframe's "Icebind" mode ahead of its Oct. 7th, 2026 launch
items.content:
0 Push your Loadouts to their limit and tackle objectives via six-player Squads in a new innovative, multi-stage game mode known as The Icebind! Warframe Creative Director Rebecca Ford walks you through it ahead of its launch on all platforms October 7.

Previously announced as “Glacial Defiance,” The Icebind offers Missions designed for veteran Tenno itching to take on larger group experiences that require increased coordination — along with superior skills and firepower. This is something of an experiment for us, but rest assured we’ll be monitoring feedback from the community closely as we continue to iterate on it going forward.

Originally borne from an idea by @WarframeFlo, The Icebind is accessible via Cephalon Melica atop Yuvan Peak by expending Cryobells — keys that include randomized enemies, locations, Mission types and Modifiers. Your Squad of six will vote on which to play, where Level 999+ foes and challenging Mission restrictions await. Tough it out and you’re guaranteed a Riven Splicer along with other Rewards, including bonuses for completing additional Side Objectives.

Please note: The Icebind can only be entered up to three times per week.

Direct an issue or corrections to the author. Abuse/misuse of this feature carries penalties.

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.

items.title: The Iceblade of Narin in Warframe Was a Disappointment – Opinion
items.summary: The Iceblade of Narin update in Warframe falls short as a final update in 2026 leading into Tau at the end of the year.
items.content:
Okay, what happened here? Because 2026 for Warframe was big on promises and has sadly fallen short in every content drop following The Old Peace. Shadowgrapher fell off the discussion after a couple of days from its launch. In fact, it’s one of the only updates I have not written a dedicated article for due to how lackluster it was and how frustrating the game mode ended up being. Jade Shadows: Constellations revived a bit of my hope. Despite some of the narrative elements just not working out properly (and giving the only 2 protoframes that lacked depth when compared to past iterations). But now we find ourselves in quite a disappointing place with the Iceblade of Narin update that launched almost two weeks ago.

Well, outside of it being another Warframe update with a little bit of everything – a new frame, weapons, skins, etc. there’s not much else holding it together. Sure, we got a rework for Banshee and a way to lock stats on rivens when you reroll them. But when you look at even Shadowgrapher and a promise made during Devstream 197 , this update feels hollow and bitter to me. Especially when I realized this would also be the final update before things leading to Tau start on October 15th.

With all of this out in the open, I need to at least mention that I am aware that the Glacial Defiance game mode, renamed “The Icebind,” is coming in about a week after being delayed ahead of the update’s launch . This is fine, as it is an endgame activity. But not even the exciting concept of The Icebind would be enough to stave off how I feel about a few major problems with the update and how it’s been executed.

As with every major update in Warframe going as far back as Lua’s Prey. Digital Extremes has added a brand new mission with a dedicated currency that alleviated the grind for the frame in that update. You could either get lucky with drops or spend those resources to get what you’re missing. This has been tried and true for years and has worked flawlessly for Digital Extremes. The only time we have not seen this implemented is in big end-of-year expansions like Whispers in the Walls , Warframe: 1999 , and The Old Peace .

Now let’s look at how Narin and her weapons were added to this update. They now share an existing reward pool with everything in the already existing missions in the Zariman Ten-Zero. The only time you get the new currency is from eximus units that have guaranteed chances to spawn, but that’s it. There is no new mission where the warframe and weapons are tied to. This makes it so you now have to fight with low drop chances to maybe get an Aeolak part when you want a blueprint for Narin. Not to mention, I have not seen the new weapon blueprints drop at all. This means you are reliant solely on the new currency.

This is my biggest issue with the update overall. It feels like an overcorrection from Jade Shadows: Constellations, where you could reasonably get everything for Sirius, Orion, Pride, and Wrath within a day or two of casual grind sessions. As of now, I have still not received a blueprint for Narin herself from exterminations or mobile defense. It feels much more luck-reliant to get her blueprints than even Follie, Sirius, or Orion’s parts in the more recent updates.

I feel they could have easily added a new survival or even interception mission and tied the drops there, with entropic eximus units spawning frequently, but they instead chose to inject Narin’s blueprints into an existing drop table and rely on the currency to do the rest of the work. While this is a major disappointment overall, this isn’t even the biggest issue of the update, and that involves what was said in Devstream 197.

During Devstream 197, Creative Director Rebecca Ford stated that the story of the update will be tied to the choice you made during The War Within. It was not explicitly stated as a continuation or anything of the like. But this promise still rubs me the wrong way in how it was handled. That being there was no real integration or narrative elements to the update at all. In fact, I find it strange that Narin exists in the way she does and froze the moment on Yuvan Peak as she did. It just feels off. Especially with all the new Zariman posters everywhere and the console for Melica being there when it wasn’t before. Where did she come from? Why did she freeze that moment in time?

Even if past updates also faltered in warframe introductions, namely Follie at the beginning of the year, they still had some commentary and narration to listen to if you wanted to piece things together. When it comes to Narin, unless The Icebind fixes this? Which I highly doubt it will. Narin will be just another warframe to add to the roster and not much else. This is very disappointing, especially coming off updates like Jade Shadows: Constellations and Shadowgrapher that did this part better.

While Digital Extremes never explicitly stated there would be a quest of any kind, Narin is just going to remain a mystery. With only the explanation in the devstream to give her any narrative coherence to her backstory. But there’s one last part of this update that really bugs me, especially with Tau on the horizon .

I do know that we have the Epoch Operation coming on the 15th , which I will be playing. But with Tau in December (most likely). This might be the last major update for the solar system we can expect for a while. After all, we are heading to a brand new solar system as we take the next major step of the ongoing story, and Digital Extremes will be focused on fleshing Tau out. With this in mind, this initially gave me some level of expectation for Iceblade of Narin . Mentioning The War Within, and going back to the Zariman? It felt like an ominous cliffhanger in the making. But it just did not meet any of those expectations.

Combining everything above, from the lack of a dedicated game mode for the grind for Narin and her weapons. As well as the absence of any narrative coherence or integration for Narin besides what was said in the devstream. The Iceblade of Narin update just missed the mark entirely. It is very disappointing considering just how consistent Digital Extremes has been with these types of updates for years. Even last year’s update around the same time, The Vallis Undermind , had a lot more meat on its bones.

I will still be checking out The Icebind and the Epoch Operation. However, I feel like this update did not live up to the mystery and hype of its reveal. While I do like Narin and her kit (after the recent hotfix), and Nunchasa especially, I feel like there was a lot more that could have been done with this update to prevent it from feeling disappointing.

items.title: Warframe of Mind: Chilling with the Iceblade of Narin update
From Narin to Tau, 'Warframe's Next Step
items.summary: ©INVENAt the recent 'Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul,' Digital Extremes clearly showed where 'Warframe' is heading next.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ©INVEN At the recent 'Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul,' Digital Extremes clearly showed where 'Warframe' is heading next. From the Korean culture-inspired new Warframe 'Narin' to the 6-player cooperative challenge 'The Icebind,' and Tau, which had long existed only in lore—the big picture of where the game is headed was made abundantly clear.

However, not everything could be addressed on-site. Deeper topics—such as the design philosophy behind Narin, how the 6-player content differs from traditional 4-player missions, and what role Tau will play in Warframe's evolving story—could not be fully asked due to time constraints.

Following Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul, we sent several additional questions to Digital Extremes. Responding to us was Megan Everett, Community Director for Warframe. In this interview, centered on 'Iceblade of Narin,' we discussed the design direction for the new Warframe, the intentions behind 'The Icebind,' Warframe beyond Tau, and why the team has been actively highlighting the Korean community lately—delving deeper into stories that couldn't be fully covered on-site.

Narin is Warframe's first female Cold-themed Warframe. With Frost already serving as an iconic Cold Warframe, what was the most important consideration in crafting Narin's unique playstyle and identity?

Megan Everett: At Digital Extremes, we always love a good challenge. Creative Director Rebecca Ford originally had a personal goal to have a Warframe for every letter of the English alphabet. After reaching that goal, we started thinking about how we could diversify Warframes even further in fun ways.

Frost was released back in 2013 during Warframe's early days, and a very long time had passed before we revisited ice as a core theme. With Tau right on the horizon, it felt like the right moment to revisit this classic theme and create a special Warframe that complements Frost both aesthetically and gameplay-wise, while possessing a completely unique look and feel.

To achieve that, Narin's abilities and playstyle needed to be distinctly different from Frost's, while still grounding themselves in the existing mechanics of Cold elemental damage. Incorporating elements of sword dancing and skating allowed us to follow those Cold mechanics while giving Narin her own distinct identity in terms of mobility and overall gameplay feel.

Narin was designed to utilize the Cold Status Effect for both offense and defense, rather than just freezing enemies. In recent Warframe designs, are ability synergy and status effect utilization becoming even more important?

Megan Everett: Synergy is always important, though it's hard to say it's more crucial now than in the past. Above all, the thrill of discovery and fun must come first. Ability kits should remain open-ended so players can experiment with different loadouts and uncover playstyles that even we, as developers, didn't anticipate.

When combined with mods, weapons, armor sets, and other customization options, players can create builds so freely that they even surprise their own squadmates. We absolutely love seeing that happen in Warframe.

Narin heavily incorporates elements inspired by Korean culture. Beyond adopting superficial design motifs, what process did you go through to seamlessly integrate Korean imagery into the Warframe universe?

Megan Everett: Cultural inspiration is immensely important to everyone at Digital Extremes. We want to create content that diverse players can connect with in different ways. To do that, you can't just use a few colors or patterns. For something to truly resonate with people, you have to push yourself beyond the surface level across narrative, gameplay, character design, and many other aspects.

It's crucial that how deeply we care shows through in a meaningful way. It needs to be crafted with responsibility and love, and ultimately, it must always feel like it naturally belongs in the Warframe universe.

We draw inspiration from so many things—media, culture, history—the list is endless.

items.content:
Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable Sound Team reverberates across the three tracks comprising this release. Drawing inspiration from a traditional Korean musical style called Sanjo, each song evokes the powerful, dynamic movements of a sword dancer — just like our 66th Warframe, Narin. The melodies recorded for Neote's Dance also inspired the vocals in Ice Speaker, which further combines familiar tunes associated with both the Zariman and the Man in the Wall for a unique aural motif befitting the narrative strands threaded through our latest update (as well as the intensity of the upcoming Glacial Defiance game mode).

items.title: Warframe: Banshee Prime Build and Post Rework Review
items.summary: Banshee's little rework in the most recent update in Warframe is very nice and makes her pretty viable in all forms of content in game.
items.content:
In the most recent update for Warframe, the Iceblade of Narin , one of the oldest warframes in the game, got a slight touch-up to her abilities. This streamlined her for more accessibility to what she can bring to the table. Banshee has always been in a weird spot, as players who know how to use her can make her dangerous, but most players (me included) didn’t understand her properly; this one touch-up made her easier to understand and, as such, gave her a new lease on life. So much so that I finally picked her back up and figured her out. Below will be our site’s recommended build for her in 2026.

Below is the build for her, which uses no forma, as I am using her Prime variant. If you are using the normal Banshee you got for free, simply copy what you see below with the forma you need to spend:

To get one thing out of the way quickly, I subsumed her 4th ability for Cyte-09’s Evade ability. This gives her invisibility to synergize with her other abilities so long as you keep getting headshot kills. From here, it’s pretty standard, just mostly build for a balance of each stack, with most of it going to range. Just make sure to add Arcane Crepuscular from the Hex’s shop in 1999.

Below are the Archon Shards I landed on for her. These are purely for flavor, and you can swap them out for whatever you wish.

As stated previously, the touch-up to her abilities is quite nice. You aren’t rooted in place, and everything feels much easier to understand with her abilities. I do respect the decision they made not to completely rework her kit. Especially if we look at past reworks like Oberon’s. But this little touch-up made me enjoy using her more. I would highly recommend using the Dual Torxica with this build. This is due to the fact that those pistols give lingering cold procs to random enemies, slowing them down so you can hit the weak points created with Sonar. It’s a killer build for Steel Path and beyond in Warframe.

items.title: Warframe: Nunchasa Build and Review
items.summary: The Nunchasa is a sleek, stylish and strong new bow in warframe. This article will be our recommended build and overall review of it!
items.content:
The Iceblade of Narin update has been filled with many misses, but that cannot be applied to the new weapons and Narin herself. Including the Nunchasa, a new Ice-focused bow that is just flat-out fun and great to use in all levels of content. It’s cool (pun intended), strong, and very stylish. Below will be our recommended build and review for it in Warframe!

Below will be our recommended build for the Nunchasa, which will need 3 formas altogether:

Nunchasa is a very critical-focused weapon, so a cocktail of the usual mods to play it into that goes well with how the weapon performs. I strongly encourage Hunter Munitions and Primary Deadhead to ensure each pull of the bow and aiming at the head pays off. Trust me, you will need it in higher levels of content.

I have practically zero complaints about the Nunchasa in Warframe . It’s the first bow in a long time with its own unique quirk that really needed a fire rate mod to enhance. When you get enough hits with it, you can let loose a special charged shot that deals very good damage to adds in a straight line. Not to mention it looks absolute sick to boot. I strongly encourage farming the Zariman for the Entropic Kuva to earn it; trust me.

Disclaimer – Digital Extremes provided Nunchasa for usage in this article.

Citrine Prime dazzles in the latest Prime Access release! Gilded in radiant Orokin filigree, Citrine Prime arrives alongside her multifaceted signature Prime Weapons and Prime Accessories. https://store.steampowered.com/app/5131900/Warframe_Citrine_Prime_Access__Weapons_Pack/ https://store.steampowered.com/app/5131910/Warframe_Citrine_Prime_Access__Accessories_Pack/ https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/87981/Warframe_Citrine_Prime_Access__Prime/ https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/87980/Warframe_Citrine_Prime_Access__Complete/

Citrine Prime Access includes:

Citrine Prime

The crystalline citadel ascends. Citrine Prime captivates with refined radiance, her brilliant gems set within the finest gold filigree.

Steflos Prime

This rose has gilded thorns. Deal death from even further afar with Citrine Prime’s signature shotgun.

Corufell Prime

Corufell Prime’s golden vines streamline its transformation for even faster Heavy Attacks.

Exclusive Citrine Prime Glyphs

Citrine Prime Accessories

  • Sphatika Prime Syandana
  • Spinele Prime Operator/Drifter Accessories
  • Alumeti Prime Sugatra
  • Prismatic Gem Prime Decoration
  • 90-Day Affinity Booster
  • 90-Day Resource Booster

WHAT ARE PRIMES?

When you require the finest and most powerful armaments, only Primes will do. Exquisitely gilded, every Prime Warframe, Weapon and item exists in its purest form — just as the Orokin intended.
